---
title: "METIS"
---

METIS turns a bank of simulator runs into a neural surrogate you can train,
evaluate, save and use in notebooks, fitting scripts or dashboards.

[Start with a complete example](package/quickstart.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Configure runs with Hydra](package/hydra.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary}

## One library and two useful entry points

Use Python objects when working interactively or embedding a model in an
application. Use Hydra to compose experiment configurations, override settings
and run sweeps. Both call the same training and evaluation functions and save
the same model artifacts.

## From simulations to trustworthy predictions

1. [Read and validate your simulation bank](package/data.qmd).
2. Train an MLP baseline, then compare model families relevant to your goal.
3. [Evaluate withheld trajectories in original units](package/evaluation.qmd).
4. [Save and reload the model in another process](package/deployment.qmd).
5. Inspect errors and coverage before choosing where to simulate next.

The library supports deterministic prediction (MLP and autoregressive
transformer) and stochastic trajectories (flow matching and normalising flow).
An evaluable flow density can support approximate-likelihood fitting.
Generated variability is not uncertainty about surrogate accuracy.

CPU training works by default. CUDA is optional in the package API; the
historical advanced source trainer supports CUDA/DDP and sequence conditioning.
The new high-level API currently targets static inputs and fixed time grids.

## Installation

~~~bash
python -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
python -m pip install "metis-surrogate @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
metis demo --steps 100 --output metis-demo
~~~

Python 3.11+ is supported. The import is `metis`; the distribution is
`metis-surrogate`. This project is not yet published on PyPI, and the existing
PyPI `metis` package is unrelated.

## Development and provenance

The original model implementations, diagrams and advanced recipes are retained
in the background sections. The package workflow is the recommended starting
point for a new researcher. The repository is MIT licensed, with attribution
and third-party notices preserved.
